name: Gertrude Mary Cox
summary: American statistician and pioneer in experimental design and statistics education.

name: Iowa State College
summary: Land-grant university in Iowa where Cox received her training.

name: North Carolina State College
summary: University in Raleigh where Cox established the Department of Experimental Statistics.

name: University of North Carolina
summary: State university system that incorporated the Institute of Statistics.

name: Research Triangle Institute
summary: Non-profit research organization where Cox served as first director of the Statistics Research Division.

aliases: Cairo University Institute of Statistical Studies and Researches
name: Institute of Statistical Studies and Researches
summary: Statistics institute at Cairo University where Cox consulted in 1964.

name: Ford Foundation
summary: Philanthropic foundation that funded Cox's consulting work in Egypt.

name: International Statistical Institute
summary: International professional organization for statisticians where Cox served as treasurer and committee chair.

name: American Statistical Association
summary: Professional association for statisticians in the United States which Cox presided over.

name: Institute of Mathematical Statistics
summary: Professional organization for mathematical statisticians that elected Cox a fellow.

name: William G. Cochran
summary: Statistician who co-authored the textbook Experimental Designs with Gertrude Cox.

name: George Snedecor
summary: Director of the statistics program at Iowa State and Cox's graduate advisor.

name: Harold Hotelling
summary: Prominent mathematical statistician who served as associate director under Cox.

name: Dayton
summary: Town in Iowa where Gertrude Cox was born.

name: Cairo
summary: Capital city of Egypt where Cox worked as a consultant.

name: Experimental Designs
summary: Textbook on experimental design co-authored by Cox and Cochran.
